site.name: Grand Republic Mine
site.location: Sunshine Gulch / Gold Hill Mining District
overview: Grand Republic Mine is a documented historic gold-, silver-, and tungsten-producing mine in Sunshine Gulch southeast of Gold Hill.
Federal and Colorado mining records describe substantial underground development and production, making the site suitable for fuller visitor history rather than identification-only treatment.

timeline.text: The Grand Republic was developed in the Gold Hill district as a precious-metal mine with an adit, inclined shaft, and multiple drift levels.
Gold Hill district reporting recorded broad low-grade gold ore bodies at the Grand Republic and identified the mine among the district's established workings.
A U.S. Geological Survey examination documented the surface area and mine dumps; the underground workings were inaccessible during that visit.

moreHistory: USGS Trace Elements Investigations Report 59 places the Grand Republic in Sunshine Gulch about 2.75 miles southeast of Gold Hill and summarizes earlier federal work on the property.

The federal description credits the mine with more than $100,000 in chiefly gold-and-silver output and more than $80,000 in tungsten ore, while documenting about 2,000 feet of workings developed by an adit, inclined shaft, and drifts on several levels.

Gold Hill district geologic reporting also records wide low-grade gold ore bodies at the Grand Republic. The mapped mine-level coordinate is used for identification; Remnant does not claim that it is a field-surveyed surviving portal or shaft collar.
